manufacture: Extruded/anodized aluminum sliding-sash sill assembly represented as a sloped closed tray section plus a separately formed exterior skirt and projecting drip nose. Two front drainage openings are real gaps between skirt segments; their dark appearance must arise from the recessed tray edge and scene lighting rather than painted black pixels.
dimensionsThickness: Benchmark dimensional assumptions: sill width 2.460 m; tray depth 0.195 m; tray thickness 0.020 m; 0.008 m outward fall across the tray; exterior skirt height 0.044 m and depth 0.018 m; drip nose 0.012 m high x 0.032 m deep; two 0.050 m drain openings centered at x +/-0.620 m; approximately 0.023 m physical recess behind each drain opening; approximately 0.008 m controlled seat into the existing lower frame interface. These values are not presented as dimensions of an identified commercial model.
materialsFinish: Canonical MAT_AgedAluminum only. Formal material microstructure uses Standard metallic workflow with mapped metallic 0.82-0.94, roughness 0.43-0.55, tangent-space normal microstructure and opaque depth-writing response. No emissive energy, painted highlights, black-hole decals or texture-only drainage slots.
mounting: Each sill assembly is aligned to one existing HD_BayAssembly and replaces only the enabled HD_WindowSillDrip renderer. The back of the tray seats under the lower aluminum sash frame by approximately 8 mm; the exterior skirt and drip nose project toward +Z, the camera-facing/weather side of the benchmark facade. Existing sash, glazing gasket and lock assemblies remain separate.
interfacesGapsSeals: The lower frame bears on the tray rather than floating above it. The tray front terminates approximately 23 mm behind the exterior skirt, so the two 50 mm skirt interruptions reveal a real recessed drainage path. Skirt edges are physical geometry with millimetric chamfers. The continuous lower drip nose projects beyond the skirt to encourage water release away from the facade face. No coplanar painted cutouts are permitted.
orientationExposure: Exterior +Z face and upward tray receive midsummer sun, rain and sky fill; the recessed drain openings receive less direct sky and should become darker by occlusion/contact response. Benchmark render state is dry, so current wetness is zero even though aging metadata records long-term rain exposure.
aging: Cause-based ordinary exposure only: UV/oxide broadening on anodized aluminum, dust/water spotting on the upward tray, concentrated residue near actual drainage exits, and slightly cleaner washed paths where runoff is physically possible. No ferrous rust is assigned to the aluminum sill itself.
geometryVsMaterial: Tray fall, 20 mm physical thickness, skirt segmentation, 50 mm drain openings, recess depth, chamfered edges and drip-nose projection are geometry. Fine extrusion-oriented grain, oxide microtexture, very fine scratches and filtered roughness variation belong to the material. Illumination, drain darkness and specular streaks may not be baked into albedo.
lodPolicy: LOD0 uses five renderers so tray/skirt/nose surfaces can carry explicit cause-based metadata. LOD1, LOD2 and LOD3 consolidate the same manufactured silhouette and the same two drainage openings into one combined renderer; topology is deliberately retained rather than collapsing to a slab. All four levels use animated cross-fade at 0.055/0.025/0.010/0.004 screen-relative thresholds. Actual pop/shimmer clearance requires sealed temporal 4K evidence.
weatheringCausality: Rain reaches the upward tray, follows the 8 mm outward fall, accumulates residue preferentially near the two physical front drainage exits, then separates at the projecting drip nose. Sun/UV acts strongest on exposed top/front aluminum. Recess grime is permitted only where geometry creates shelter. The benchmark remains dry with wetness=0.
lookdevBrief: Front view: two 50 mm drain openings must read as small real gaps in the skirt, not black paint; repeated sill geometry may be product-identical but the eight metric-UV cut phases must prevent synchronized microtexture. Oblique view: confirm the lower frame physically seats onto the tray and the skirt/nose projects outward without floating/interpenetration. Grazing view: confirm continuous anodized-metal highlight response across tray/skirt/nose, no slab-like razor edge, no fake highlight, and a physically darker recess behind each opening. Temporal oblique: confirm the five-renderer LOD0 and combined LOD1/2/3 remain visually coincident with no silhouette/highlight snap.
sourceBasis: Functional principle only: YKK AP technical watertightness guidance describes sliding-sash lower-frame water management and pressure/drainage approaches, while LIXIL PRESEA-H documentation confirms contemporary RC-building sliding-window systems with explicit watertight performance and aluminum sash construction. These sources support the need for a real lower-frame drainage path and seals; they do not establish the benchmark dimensions above. Sources reviewed 2026-09-12.

material.albedo: Canonical material base color floats approximately (0.55, 0.57, 0.56); no illumination or drainage darkness baked into base color.
material.specularFresnel: Unity Standard metallic BRDF; grazing reflectance must emerge from physical angular response and the reflection environment, never from a painted rim.
material.normalScale: _BumpScale=1.0; generated anodized-aluminum source profile normalStrength=0.52 before tangent-space encoding.
material.microstructure: Fine extrusion-oriented grain plus secondary irregularity; mapped texture tiling is 14 repeats per metre-scale UV unit with trilinear mipmapping/aniso as defined by detail_material_microstructure_contract.json.
material.uvAging: Eight deterministic physical-UV cut phases at 0.017 m increments decorrelate repeated windows; long-term UV/rain effects remain cause metadata/material response, not lighting baked into texture.
material.angularFresnelResponse: Metallic surface must broaden under aged roughness while retaining coherent grazing response; chrome-like sparkle or dielectric-looking flatness is a rendered failure.
